plan: [ This auction is strategically equivalent to a second‑price auction: the winner pays the highest competing bid (the clock price when others exit). The dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit. Overbidding risks paying above value; underbidding risks missing profitable wins. With no learning across rounds, I bid exactly my value: 47.0. ]

[ This is effectively a second‑price auction: the highest sealed bid wins and pays the second‑highest (clock stops at runner‑up’s bid). With independent private values and risk neutrality, the dominant strategy to maximize expected profit is to bid my true value. Overbidding risks negative profit if I win above value; underbidding risks losing positive surplus when others’ bids fall between my bid and value. No prior history to adapt to in round 1. Therefore, bid exactly my value, respecting $0.1 increments. ]

[ This is effectively a second‑price (English) auction with sealed exit prices. With independent private values (uniform 0–49) and three bidders, the dominant strategy is to bid truthfully. Bidding below 36 risks missing profitable wins when competitors’ bids fall between the shaded bid and 36. Bidding above 36 risks negative payoff if the second-highest bid exceeds 36. Ties are random; truthful bidding still maximizes expected profit. No cross-round learning applies (1 round). Therefore, set the sealed bid equal to my value so I win exactly when it’s profitable and pay the second-highest bid. ]
